key_insight: The paper defines semi-local wall coordinates and transformed velocities with elliptic equations, so compressibility and wall heat transfer are built into the transformation before extracting wall-normal profiles.
engineering_relevance: This gives a more physically consistent inner scaling for high-speed and thermally driven wall-bounded flows, improving comparison across cooled boundary layers and channel configurations.
method: Form a semi-local wall coordinate from local density and viscosity scaling.
Solve a Helmholtz-type elliptic equation for a bounded density-induced correction to wall-normal stretching.
Use projection equations to compute transformed coordinate Y+ and projected velocity U+ from mean flow, density, viscosity, wall distance, and wall normals.
evidence_signal: A single calibrated set of wall-layer constants from two cooled flat-plate cases was applied to zero-pressure-gradient boundary layers and to isothermal and mixed thermal-wall channels, with improved inner and buffer-layer placement reported in the abstract.
watch_item: The approach depends on solving elliptic equations and on the chosen wall-normal/density inputs, so implementation consistency and boundary treatment may matter in complex geometries.
paper_title: Semi-local transformation for compressible wall turbulence via elliptic equations
